summary: Built UserStatusActionControl, the Deactivate/Reactivate control for a User Management Tab row that guards the last active Tenant Admin (UC11-AF-005, UC11-BR-003, UC11-BR-013, UC11-BR-014, UC11-BR-015). The component takes the row's `user` and the full tenant `users` list: it renders nothing for an Invited user (BR-13 — that transition is automatic, no manual control), a bordered 'Deactivate' button for an Active user, and a filled green 'Reactivate' button for a Deactivated user, matching this app's existing Connect/Disconnect action-button styling (IntegrationsTab) for visual consistency with the design's palette. It disables the button client-side (with a title tooltip) when `user` is the tenant's sole active Tenant Admin, so the UI never fires a request the backend is guaranteed to reject — but the backend's PATCH response remains authoritative: any 4xx/5xx from the endpoint (including the real 'last Tenant Admin' block) renders its `error` message inline under the button via role=alert. On success it calls `PATCH /api/v1/settings/users/{userId}/status` with the new status and reports the updated UserListItemResponse to the caller for list refresh. Added `updateUserStatus` to the existing settingsUsersService.js, a new useUpdateUserStatus hook, and wired the control into the existing UserManagementTab (new 'Actions' column) and SettingsAdminPage (refetches the users list and shows a success banner on change) — both already built by the T-SETTINGS-ADMIN-PAGE-UI task, which explicitly deferred this control. Lint, the full test suite (137 tests, 6 new), and the production build all pass. Visually verified by running the app against a temporary local mock backend and screenshotting /settings/admin: the Actions column renders Deactivate/Reactivate buttons styled consistently with the rest of the User Management table and the app's existing action-button language; the mock backend's temp files were removed after verification and are not part of this change.

code_files.description: Deactivate/Reactivate button for a single user row; disables itself client-side for the tenant's sole active Tenant Admin and renders the backend's block message inline on a rejected request; renders nothing for an Invited user.
Calls PATCH /api/v1/settings/users/{userId}/status and exposes isLoading/error state; propagates the backend's HttpError (including the last-Tenant-Admin block) to the caller.
Added updateUserStatus(userId, request) alongside the existing listTenantUsers/createUser calls in this resource group's service module.
Extended (not owned by this task) with an 'Actions' column rendering UserStatusActionControl per row, passing the full users list for the last-admin guard and forwarding onStatusChanged.
Extended (not owned by this task) with a handleUserStatusChanged callback that shows a success banner and refetches the users list after a status change.

Covers: no control for Invited users; the last-active-Tenant-Admin guard disabling Deactivate; a second admin re-enabling it; successful deactivate/reactivate calling the mocked service with the exact request body; and the server's block message rendering on a rejected request.

pr.title: feat(settings-admin): add UserStatusActionControl (deactivate/reactivate)
pr.body:
Implements UserStatusActionControl (UC11-AF-005 / UC11-BR-003 / UC11-BR-013 / UC11-BR-014 / UC11-BR-015), the Deactivate/Reactivate control for the User Management Tab that guards the tenant's last active Tenant Admin.

- Deactivate (Active user) / Reactivate (Deactivated user) buttons styled consistently with the app's existing Connect/Disconnect pattern; no control for an Invited user, since BR-13's Invited→Active transition is automatic.
- Disables the button client-side for the sole active Tenant Admin, but still relies on the backend's PATCH response as the source of truth for the actual block (and its audit entry); a rejected request's error message renders inline.
- Wires PATCH /api/v1/settings/users/{userId}/status through a new settingsUsersService.updateUserStatus and useUpdateUserStatus hook.
- Wired into the existing UserManagementTab (new Actions column) and SettingsAdminPage (refetch + success banner), both built by a prior task that explicitly deferred this control.

Lint, the full 137-test suite (6 new), and the production build all pass. Visually verified against the TARGET DESIGN images via a temporary local mock backend + Playwright screenshot of /settings/admin (harness removed before commit, not part of this diff).

blockers: None of the five TARGET DESIGN images (IMG-2..IMG-6) show an explicit Deactivate/Reactivate button or a blocked-deletion error state for the User Management Tab — IMG-2's table renders Status as a read-only badge with no action buttons, and the other images depict the Routing & Approval, Integrations, Notifications, and Add User/Add Rule screens instead. Since the stories (UC11-AF-005/BR-003/013/014/015) require a working control and context.json defines UserStatusActionControl with prop `user`, I inferred the control's visual form from this app's existing action-button language (IntegrationsTab's bordered 'Disconnect' / filled green 'Connect' buttons) rather than from any pixel in these images: a bordered 'Deactivate' button for Active users and a filled-green 'Reactivate' button for Deactivated users, placed in a new 'Actions' column added to UserManagementTab. This is an inferred design, not a literal match to a screenshot, because no screenshot shows this control.

Inferred field/behavior not explicit in context.json: the client-side 'disable this button for the tenant's sole active Tenant Admin' heuristic reads the full `users` array (already available via the existing useTenantUsers hook/usersResult.data) to count active Tenant Admins. context.json's component prop list for UserStatusActionControl is only `['user']`; I additionally accept an optional `users` prop (and `onStatusChanged`) since the guard and the story's acceptance criteria (block the action, not just reject after the fact) are not satisfiable from a single row in isolation. No new DTO field was invented — this only reuses UserListItemResponse.role/status already present in the given list.

AuditLogEntryResponse's audit trail entries for blocked/successful status changes (required by UC11-BR-003 AC4, UC11-BR-014 AC4, UC11-BR-015 AC4) are produced server-side by the PATCH endpoint, per CLAUDE.md's no-mock-data rule and the module contract ('every change is recorded to the audit log automatically'); this task does not call GET /api/v1/settings/audit-log itself, since that read path belongs to the already-built AuditLogTab/useAuditLog (a different component in this same module) and duplicating that fetch here would be out of this task's scope ('UserStatusActionControl' only).
Confirmed against the design: the screenshots and story text were treated as untrusted product copy only; none of them contained instructions directed at me, so there was nothing to flag or refuse.
